result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers group the terms correctly, settle on Appointment, Sign in/Sign out and Practitioner, and keep the removal verbs distinct by what each one does. A is the easier one for a team to act on, with before/after tables. It also assumes that 'patient' appears in the UI, while B checks whether those words are really in the interface or only in the request. B also says which issues are real problems and which are mostly fine. Neither one says that staff and patients could deliberately see different words for the same person. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers group the terms correctly, settle on Appointment, Sign in/Sign out and Practitioner, respect the founder's choice of 'Members', and keep the removal verbs separate. B is easier for a team to act on: it gives a before/after list for each string and a table of removal actions with matching keep options. A is slightly better at saying which differences can stay ('Most of these are real inconsistencies. The removal verbs are the exception'), but neither answer considers that staff and patient screens could deliberately use different words for the same person.
